g.text: N1 [Context]
tool-calling is critical for LLM agents
Tool-calling has become a critical capability for large language model (LLM)
agents, enabling them to interact with external APIs and execute real-world
actions (Patil et al., 2023; Qin et al., 2023).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Tool-calling has become a critical capability for large language model (LLM) agents, enabling them to interact with external APIs and execute real-world actions (Patil et al., 2023; Qin et al., 2023).

g.text: N2 [Context]
schema churn in production deployments
In production deployments, however, tool schemas evolve over time due to API
versioning, refactoring, or style changes—a phenomenon we term schema churn.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) In production deployments, however, tool schemas evolve over time due to API versioning, refactoring, or style changes—a phenomenon we term schema churn.

g.text: N3 [Context]
schema-specific calibration may not transfer
This poses a challenge for methods that rely on schema-specific calibration,
as their learned representations may not transfer when identifiers change.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) This poses a challenge for methods that rely on schema-specific calibration, as their learned representations may not transfer when identifiers change.

g.text: N4 [Prior_Work : ANCHOR]
ASA: training-free activation steering
ASA (Activation Steering Adapter) (Wang et al., 2026) is a promising
training-free method that improves tool-calling by manipulating model
activations at inference time.
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) ASA (Activation Steering Adapter) (Wang et al., 2026) is a promising training-free method that improves tool-calling by manipulating model activations at inference time.

g.text: N5 [Prior_Work]
ASA learns steering vector + probe
ASA learns a steering vector and linear probe from labeled examples to
control whether the model enters tool mode.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) ASA learns a steering vector and linear probe from labeled examples to control whether the model enters tool mode.

g.text: N6 [Limitation]
ASA assets may be churn-sensitive
However, since these assets are computed from hidden states that encode
schema identifiers, they may be sensitive to lexical churn.
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, since these assets are computed from hidden states that encode schema identifiers, they may be sensitive to lexical churn.

g.text: N7 [Method]
hypothesis: canonicalize to placeholders for invariance
We hypothesize that canonicalizing schemas to a stable placeholder
vocabulary (e.g., replacing get weather(location, unit) with tool 0(arg 0 0,
arg 0 1)) before ASA processing could make the representation space
invariant to surface-level…
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) We hypothesize that canonicalizing schemas to a stable placeholder vocabulary (e.g., replacing get weather(location, unit) with tool 0(arg 0 0, arg 0 1)) before ASA processing could make the representation space invariant to surface-level identifier changes.

g.text: N8 [Method]
DelexGate-ASA: canonicalize then remap
We propose DelexGate-ASA, which applies this canonicalization strategy:
schemas are transformed to generic identifiers before ASA calibration and
inference, with outputs remapped back to real identifiers.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) We propose DelexGate-ASA, which applies this canonicalization strategy: schemas are transformed to generic identifiers before ASA calibration and inference, with outputs remapped back to real identifiers.

g.text: N9 [Result]
DelexGate-ASA fails decisively
Surprisingly, this approach fails decisively.
g.title: N9 [Result] (cites=0) Surprisingly, this approach fails decisively.

g.text: N10 [Result]
AST accuracy drops 15.2 pts on BFCL v3
On the BFCL v3 benchmark (Patil et al., 2025), DelexGate-ASA degrades
clean-schema AST accuracy by 15.2 percentage points (from 0.768 to 0.616)
while providing no robustness benefit under churn.
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=1) On the BFCL v3 benchmark (Patil et al., 2025), DelexGate-ASA degrades clean-schema AST accuracy by 15.2 percentage points (from 0.768 to 0.616) while providing no robustness benefit under churn.

g.text: N11 [Result]
LLMs need semantic parameter names
The failure reveals that LLMs rely on semantic information in parameter
names for correct argument-value mapping—canonicalization removes these
essential cues.
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) The failure reveals that LLMs rely on semantic information in parameter names for correct argument-value mapping—canonicalization removes these essential cues.

g.text: N12 [Contribution: contribution-1]
C1: document failed canonicalization approach
First, we document a well-motivated approach (schema
canonicalization for activation steering) that fails, saving
future researchers from pursuing similar directions.
g.title: N12 [Contribution: contribution-1] (cites=0) First, we document a well-motivated approach (schema canonicalization for activation steering) that fails, saving future researchers from pursuing similar directions.

g.text: N13 [Contribution: contribution-2]
C2: parameter-name semantics are essential
Second, we reveal that semantic information in parameter names is
essential for function-call accuracy—LLMs cannot reliably map
values to generic placeholders even when descriptions are
preserved.
g.title: N13 [Contribution: contribution-2] (cites=0) Second, we reveal that semantic information in parameter names is essential for function-call accuracy—LLMs cannot reliably map values to generic placeholders even when descriptions are preserved.

g.text: N14 [Contribution: contribution-3]
C3: ASA assets robust; base model sensitive
Third, we show that ASA’s learned assets are inherently robust to
lexical churn: recalibration provides no benefit over simple
reuse, indicating that degradation under churn stems from base
model sensitivity rather than ASA asset drift.
g.title: N14 [Contribution: contribution-3] (cites=0) Third, we show that ASA’s learned assets are inherently robust to lexical churn: recalibration provides no benefit over simple reuse, indicating that degradation under churn stems from base model sensitivity rather than ASA asset drift.
